title: Maximum Subtree of the Same Color
summary: Given a tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has a color, find the largest subtree where all nodes share the same color, rooted at node 0.
statement: Given a tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has a color, find the largest subtree where all nodes share the same color, rooted at node 0. The output is the size of this largest subtree.
constraints: edges form an undirected tree rooted at node zero and colors has one positive integer per node.
A node’s subtree contains that node and all descendants under the root-zero orientation.
Return the maximum size of a subtree whose every node has one color.
hints: A subtree is monochrome only if every child subtree is monochrome and each child root matches its parent.
Use postorder recursion returning both subtree size and a validity flag.
Combine child sizes; AND their flags and color comparisons; update the maximum only when valid.
Postorder has complete information for every descendant, and the recursive condition is exactly necessary and sufficient for the rooted subtree to share one color.
editorial: Postorder has complete information for every descendant, and the recursive condition is exactly necessary and sufficient for the rooted subtree to share one color.

tests.explanation: The root subtree mixes colors, while each leaf alone is monochrome, so the maximum is one.
The subtree rooted at node two contains three nodes, all color three.
